label: W3C DID/VC standards demonstrate that self-certifying identifiers technically enable portable, issuer-independent credential verification
UNHCR precedent of non-state identity documents plus PoH/BrightID field experience inductively support that plural vouching can substitute for state attestation

defeaters.description: The UNHCR/PoH analogy is misleading because it conflates two different trust models. UNHCR credentials work because UNHCR itself is a trusted institutional brand with decades of state-level relationships — relying parties accept the credential because they trust UNHCR, not because they trust a decentralized protocol. Proof-of-Humanity and BrightID, which are closer to the thesis's architecture, have failed to achieve meaningful institutional acceptance: no bank, government, or major aid organization accepts them. The evidence actually shows that non-state vouching works only when a single prestigious institution backstops it — precisely the single-party dependency the thesis aims to eliminate.
defeaters.response: Partially answered, with a concession. The defeater is right that PoH/BrightID — decentralized social-graph protocols — have achieved no institutional acceptance, but that is the wrong analogue: the design's Layer 3 is plural CONSTITUTED institutions (UNHCR, diaspora bodies, relief agencies, municipalities-in-exile), each a brand-backed voucher, not an anonymous web of trust. So the apt precedent is the one that works (UNHCR-type institutional attestation), and 'plural' here means several such institutions, not a protocol replacing institutions. The concession the defeater forces, and it is real: acceptance flows from institutional reputation, not from the protocol — so the design depends on recruiting already-trusted constituted bodies, and only their attestations will be honored. That re-introduces dependence on a handful of prestigious institutions and collapses back into the anchor-adoption and demand-side problems. Net: feasibility is non-zero (UNHCR-style works), but the protocol contributes portability and accountability, not acceptance; acceptance must be borrowed from institutions the design does not control.

label: Internet governance precedents (ICANN, CAs, fediverse) inductively show that multi-stakeholder commons governance raises capture cost and makes it publicly observable, though imperfectly

If portable credentials are feasible (C2), plural vouching substitutes for state attestation (C3), commons governance converts capture dynamics (C4), re-concentration is resisted (C5), and an anchor relying party exists (C6), then the full thesis follows by conjunction

defeaters.description: The conjunction argument assumes the sub-claims are largely independent, but they are deeply entangled. If the uniqueness registry re-concentrates (C5 fails), the commons governance claim (C4) also collapses — a dominant operator IS the single-party chokepoint the thesis claims to eliminate. Similarly, if no anchor relying party emerges (C6 fails), the technical validity of the credential (C2, C3) becomes moot. The sub-claims are not modular building blocks but a fragile chain where each failure mode cascades. The overall confidence should therefore be closer to the product of the sub-claim confidences than their average, making the thesis substantially weaker than any individual sub-claim suggests.
defeaters.response: Conceded — and this is the most important result of the stress test. The conditions are entangled, not independent: if the registry re-concentrates (C5), commons governance (C4) collapses because the dominant operator IS the chokepoint; if no anchor relying party emerges (C6), the technically valid credential (C2, C3) is inert. So confidence is closer to the PRODUCT of the sub-claims than their average. Product ≈ 0.85 × 0.60 × 0.55 × 0.45 × 0.58 ≈ 0.07. Even allowing partial mitigation and correlation, the honest figure is well under 50%, not the 62% the averaging shows. Narrowing the thesis into explicit conditions did not rescue it — it exposed that the design is a fragile five-link chain whose two weakest links (re-concentration resistance at 45%, anchor adoption at 58%) gate everything else.
